newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW - Thailand's EGCO to bid in power scheme.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Thailand's EGCO to bid in power scheme.

text.p: Major Thai private power producer Electricity Generating Plc will take part in bidding for the government's private power producer schemes in a move to sustain its growth, company officials said on Wednesday.

"Small Power Producer (SPP) and Independent Power Producer (IPP) schemes will be our next major interest. This will maintain our earnings growth to shareholders," Worawit Khamkanist, EGCO managing director, told Reuters.
SPP and IPP are the government's schemes to allow greater private sector participation in the country's power production.

Under the second stage of IPP scheme, the state-run Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) plans to buy about 3,300 megawatts of electricity from private producers to the national grid starting between 2003 and 2006.
"With our strong experience and expertise in the power business, we are confident to win the bidding," Worawit said.
EGCO owns and operates two major power plants in Rayong and Nakhon Si Thammarat provinces. The plants have a combined capacity of 2000 megawatts.
EGCO is majority owned by EGAT which has a 40 percent stake in the firm.

Machima Kunjara Na Ayudhya, deputy managing director, said EGCO will be more cautious about any new domestic investments this year due to unfavourable economic condition and a higher cost of funds as Thailand fights its worst economic crisis in over a decade.

"We will be very cautious for our future projects in Thailand. The downgrade of the country's ratings affected our cost of financing," Machima said. Moody's Investor Services has cut Thailand's long term and short term sovereign ratings.
Machima said EGCO had incurred rising foreign exchange losses in the second quarter following the recent baht weakness against the dollar.
"Our foreign exchange loss in the (second) quarter will be very high compared with the same period last year. It was in line with the baht's movement (against the dollar)," Machima said.
Machima said EGCO is also concerned about the baht's depreciation against the dollar due to the company's large dollar-denominated loans.
"Our revenue is stable and the expenses are under control. Our major concern is the baht's value which created the foreign exchange loss," Machima said.
EGCO currently has a net position of dollar-denominated loans totalling $375 million which had been borrowed to buy the power plants from the government, he said.
"If the baht fell by one baht against the dollar it could suddenly lead to an unrealised foreign exchange loss of 375 million baht, " he said.
